column1: # The PolyC driver's status domain currently has SIX members. The
# required route needs a SEVENTH, because the `-o-`/`-S` condition has
# no status member and the C side therefore has to decide it.
# The new member's value is DISJOINT from every existing status, action
#   57  #define WP_STATUS_OK        0   // success, or nothing to do
#   59  #define WP_STATUS_COMPILE   2   // a compile action was selected
#   60  #define WP_STATUS_ARITY     3   // an argument arity / domain violation
#   62  #define WP_STATUS_ENGINE    5   // the compile engine reported failure
# The ACTION domain and the EMISSION domain are SEPARATE domains and
# must not collide with the status domain. The emission domain is
# 0..4 and the action domain uses values from 1 upward, including
# WP_ACTION_NONE 20. The status domain's existing values 0..5 are
# already disjoint from the emission domain's 1..4 by construction
# because they are separate namespaces; the new member follows the
# same rule and is compared only against the STATUS domain.
#   the status domain's values after the extension are {0,1,2,3,4,5,6}
#   the largest PRE-EXISTING status value is 5
#   the new value 6 is therefore DISJOINT from every pre-existing
#   status value, and it is the LARGEST, so it cannot be confused
# The new member is a SOURCE VALUE in BOTH the PolyC subject and the
# C mirror. The C side does NOT invent a parallel value; it reads the
# SECTION 3 -- THE CONDITION THE DRIVER MUST DECIDE
# The C policy being moved is, verbatim from src/cli.c:
# where args->to_stdout is set by WP_DRIVER_FIELD_TO_STDOUT and
# The PolyC driver ALREADY classifies both options:
# So the driver can decide the condition from its OWN option
# classification, with no new option table, no new option name, no
# new flag test and no new arity rule.
# The condition, expressed on the driver's own terms:
#   WP_KIND_STDOUT is present in the argv
#   AND WP_KIND_ASSEMBLY is NOT present in the argv
# The status is a SINGLE value, so the mutually-exclusive CLI checks
# must be ORDERED. The driver already owns the arity-before-usage
# order inside WpDriverMapStatus. The new member joins that ordering.
#   1  WP_STATUS_ARITY       an option's value is missing
#   3  WP_STATUS_USAGE       an unknown argument is present
#   4  WP_STATUS_NO_INPUT    no input file and no action
#   5  WP_STATUS_COMPILE     a compile action was selected
#   6  WP_STATUS_ENGINE      the compile engine reported failure
#   7  WP_STATUS_OK          success, or nothing to do
# RATIONALE FOR THE POSITION, FROM THE LEGACY CLI ORDER:
# The legacy C CLI ran the checks in this order after the option loop:
# and the ARITY violation is reported from INSIDE the option loop,
# i.e. BEFORE any of them. The frozen order above reproduces that
# legacy order exactly, so the correction CHANGES NO OBSERVABLE
# BEHAVIOUR for any argv that does not also carry an unknown argument
